ogTitle: Ranong to Surat Thani: Andaman to Gulf 3-Day Plan
ogDesc: Leave Ranong's hot springs, drive across the peninsula past Khao Sok, then board a ferry at Donsak to the Gulf islands. A day-by-day travel plan.
h1:
Ranong → Surat Thani
Andaman Coast to the Gulf
intro: Ranong sits on the Andaman side, Surat Thani faces the Gulf of Thailand, and the two are separated by about 220 km of peninsula. That gap is exactly what makes this trip fun. You leave the hot-spring town in the morning, drive over the mountains through the Khao Sok rainforest, and finish at Donsak pier to cross over to Koh Samui, Phangan or Tao. We've laid it out as a 3-day, day-by-day plan with timings, stops and real prices we checked ourselves.

blocks.html: The main route runs south from Ranong on Highway 4 (Phetkasem), passing through the Takua Pa stretch of Phang Nga, then turns onto Highway 401, which cuts through Khao Sok National Park into Surat Thani city. From the city you carry on down to Donsak pier, about another hour, to cross to the islands. No private car? No problem — Ranong–Surat minivans run every hour.

Ranong to Surat Thani is around 220–230 km, roughly 3.5 hours by car or minivan if you don't stop. But this plan stops on purpose, because there's good stuff along the way — a roadside waterfall near the start and the Khao Sok forest in the middle. Blasting straight through means missing the views.

items: Ranong–Surat Thani minivan — departs Ranong bus terminal roughly every hour, around 07:00–17:00, fare about 200–250 THB, journey ~3.5 hrs, dropping you at Talat Kaset 2 in Surat city.
Self-drive — the most flexible option for this trip, since you can stop at the waterfall and Khao Sok as you like. Budget roughly 700–900 THB for fuel round trip.
Onward to Donsak pier — from Surat city it's another 65–70 km, ~1 hr, to Donsak pier. The ferry companies (Lomprayah/Raja/Seatran) run connecting minivans to the pier.
Ferry to the islands — Donsak→Koh Samui ~1.5 hrs / Donsak→Phangan ~2.5 hrs / Lomprayah's fast boat continues to Koh Tao.

blocks.title: Timing it so you make the boat
blocks.html: The last Donsak ferry is usually around 17:00–18:00. If you leave Ranong late and make several stops, you may not catch a boat the same day. That's why we have you overnight in Surat and board a morning ferry the next day — easier, and no rushing.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Ranong trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

items.label: Day trips from Ranong
items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Ranong → through the Khao Sok forest → Surat Thani

items.activity: Breakfast in Ranong before setting off
items.note: Grab morning dim sum in Ranong town — places like Pee Ton Breakfast (open 06:00–12:00) or one of the old dim sum shops in the market. Fuel up before the long drive.
If you have time, stop at the roadside Punyaban Waterfall near the start — a quick photo stop is worth it. Big parking area, restrooms on site.

items.activity: Turn onto Highway 401 through Khao Sok National Park
items.note: This is the best scenery of the whole route — limestone karsts lining both sides of the road. Slow down and take it in.
There are several made-to-order eateries and roadside cafés along Highway 401 — a good moment to stretch your legs.

items.activity: Arrive in Surat Thani city, check in
items.note: Pick a place in town where food is an easy walk away. Rest up before the ferry tomorrow.

items.activity: Walk San Chao Market for evening street food
items.note: Surat's famous street-food market, open afternoon into the evening — crab curry noodles, fried chicken, khanom jeen, plenty of good eats.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Surat Thani → ferry from Donsak → Gulf islands

items.activity: Surat breakfast — try southern-style crab curry noodles
items.note: Surat is known for khanom jeen. Several shops in town open early, with rich southern-style sauce that really packs a punch.
About an hour from the city. If you book a ferry-with-transfer package, the ferry company picks you up at your accommodation — easier than sorting your own ride.

items.activity: Board the ferry/fast boat at Donsak
items.note: Choose by your island destination: Donsak→Samui ~1.5 hrs / →Phangan ~2.5 hrs. Lomprayah's fast boat continues to Koh Tao.

items.activity: Arrive at your island, check in
items.note: Samui suits anyone who wants full amenities, Phangan is for partying and quiet beaches, Tao is for diving.

items.activity: Start the island trip your way
items.note: Hit the beach, swim, or go snorkeling. Make today an easy first day of island life — no need to rush.

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Enjoy the island, then plan the way back

items.activity: A full day of sea activities
items.note: An island-hopping tour to Koh Taen, Koh Nang Yuan, or diving — depending on the island you chose.

items.activity: Relax on the beach, find your photo spots
items.note: Don't cram the last day. Give the sea some of your time.
Go back the same way — ferry to Donsak, then onward by road — or fly out of Samui Airport if you chose Samui as your destination. Flexible either way.

blocks.text: Stops and standout eats along the way

blocks.html: Here's our shortlist, ordered the way you'll meet them on the route from Ranong all the way to the islands. We've added rough prices and opening hours where we could check. These change with the season, so confirm again before you go to be sure.

items.name: Dim sum breakfast in Ranong town
items.blurb: Start the day with hot Ranong-style dim sum — shumai, char siu, pork blood soup. Morning eating is a part of this town's culture. Fuel up before the long drive.

items.name: Punyaban Waterfall
items.blurb: A roadside waterfall on Highway 4 just before you leave Ranong. Pull over for photos with no long walk needed — big parking area, restrooms and shops. Best flow in the rainy season.
items.meta: Roadside on Highway 4 · near Ranong town

items.name: Limestone karst views on Highway 401, Khao Sok
items.blurb: The prettiest part of driving across the peninsula — limestone karsts lining both sides of the road through Khao Sok National Park. Drive slow and roll the windows down.

items.name: Cheow Lan Lake raft trip (optional)
items.blurb: If you have a spare day, turn into Khao Sok and overnight on a raft house on the emerald lake. Park entry is 30 THB. It's a detour plenty of people happily make because it's worth it.
items.meta: Khao Sok park · requires leaving the main route

items.name: San Chao Market, Surat Thani
items.blurb: Surat's well-known downtown street-food market — rich crab curry noodles, crispy-skin fried chicken, rice with curry, khanom jeen. An easy place to graze for dinner.

items.name: Southern-style crab curry khanom jeen
items.blurb: A Surat specialty — rich, boldly seasoned sauce. Several shops in town open from morning into the afternoon, and some let you refill the sauce. Easy on the wallet too.

items.name: Surat Thani oysters
items.blurb: Surat is known for big oysters. Seafood restaurants in town and around Kanchanadit serve large ones — eat them fresh with southern-style condiments.

items.name: Old-school restaurants in Surat city
items.blurb: Want a sit-down feast? There are several long-running Chinese-seafood restaurants. Standouts include sour curry with sea bass and turmeric-fried featherback fish — a good dinner before the ferry.

items.name: Donsak pier, where island life begins
items.blurb: The gateway to the Gulf islands, with cafés and snacks while you wait for the boat. Arrive about half an hour before your sailing so you're not scrambling at check-in.
items.meta: Donsak district · ~1 hr from the city
items.price: Ferry fare from ฿car+person, varies by sailing

blocks.text: Pick the island that fits your style

blocks.html: Once you've crossed to the Gulf side, there are three main islands from Donsak — Samui, Phangan and Tao. Each has its own character. Pick based on the kind of trip you want.

items.name: Koh Samui
items.blurb: The big island with full amenities — Chaweng and Lamai beaches, loads of restaurants and cafés, and an airport so you can fly home. Good for families and anyone who wants comfort.

items.name: Koh Phangan
items.blurb: Home to both the Full Moon party scene and quiet beaches on the north side. This island balances fun and chill, ideal if you want both modes in one place.

items.name: Koh Tao
items.blurb: The Gulf's diving capital — cheap dive courses, lots of dive sites, and the gorgeous Koh Nang Yuan. You'll need to take Lomprayah's fast boat one more leg to get here.

blocks.title: Book the ferry ahead in high season
blocks.html: In high season (Nov–Apr) and on long weekends, boats to Samui and Phangan fill up fast. Booking online with Lomprayah, Raja Ferry or Seatran in advance gives you peace of mind, especially if you're taking a car across too.

faq.q: How long does Ranong to Surat Thani take?
faq.a: It's around 220–230 km, roughly 3.5 hours by minivan or car if you don't stop. But if you stop for the waterfall and the Khao Sok views as in this plan, budget the whole day.

faq.q: Can I do this without a private car?
faq.a: Yes. Ranong–Surat Thani minivans leave Ranong bus terminal roughly every hour, around 07:00–17:00, fare about 200–250 THB, dropping you at Talat Kaset 2 in Surat city. From there you can catch a ferry-company minivan to Donsak pier.

faq.q: Which pier do I take the island ferry from in Surat?
faq.a: The main pier is Donsak, about 65–70 km from Surat city, around 1 hour away. Lomprayah, Raja Ferry and Seatran all run from there to Koh Samui, Phangan and on to Koh Tao.

faq.q: Should I overnight in Surat before the ferry?
faq.a: We recommend one night, because the last ferry is usually around 17:00–18:00. If you leave Ranong and make several stops, you often won't catch a boat the same day. Overnighting in Surat and taking a morning ferry the next day is easier.

faq.q: What's worth stopping for along the way?
faq.a: Near the start there's Punyaban Waterfall on the roadside near Ranong town. Mid-route you pass the limestone karst views on Highway 401 through Khao Sok. If you have a spare day, turn into Khao Sok to overnight on a raft house at Cheow Lan Lake. Once in Surat city, there's San Chao Market and crab curry khanom jeen to try.
